exhibits.title: After the Rain
exhibits.caption: The sidewalks were still shining when the café lights came on. We walked the long way back.
exhibits.alt: A red café awning and gold window lights reflected in a wet Paris sidewalk

exhibits.title: A Table for Two
exhibits.caption: We ordered another round of coffee so we could stay at that little table a while longer.
exhibits.alt: Two espresso cups on a café table in dappled sunlight

exhibits.title: The First Light
exhibits.caption: The river was quiet that morning. From the bridge we watched the city wake up one window at a time.
exhibits.alt: An old stone bridge across the Seine in the soft light of dawn

exhibits.title: A Road Through Provence
exhibits.caption: We pulled over for the lavender and stayed until the shadows reached across the road.
exhibits.alt: Rows of purple lavender beside tall cypress trees

exhibits.title: The Open Window
exhibits.caption: We could hear the street through the curtains. Someone downstairs was setting tables for lunch.
exhibits.alt: Cream curtains beside a sunlit open window

exhibits.title: Market Day
exhibits.caption: We bought peaches from the last stall and carried them home in the bottom of the bag.
exhibits.alt: Two ripe peaches and rumpled linen on a wooden counter

exhibits.title: Where the Land Ends
exhibits.caption: From the far end of the harbor, the houses looked small enough to hold in a hand.
exhibits.alt: Pastel houses above a calm Mediterranean harbor

exhibits.title: The Train Home
exhibits.caption: We watched the station lights stretch into the rain as the train pulled away.
exhibits.alt: Amber lights seen through a rain-streaked train window at blue hour

exhibits.title: A Slow Afternoon
exhibits.caption: We left the bicycle in the shade and sat around the corner until the sun moved across the wall.
exhibits.alt: A bicycle beside a faded terracotta wall in the shade of a tree

exhibits.title: The Story Is Still Being Written
exhibits.caption: The sun went down while we were still sitting there. There’s a letter for you here.
exhibits.alt: The sun setting over the ocean between two dark headlands

letterParagraphs: Some places are easy to remember because of what we saw. This one is easy to remember because of how long we stayed.
I keep thinking about the small rituals we made without deciding to. The second cup. The window seat. The walk that took twice as long as it should have.
If I could keep one afternoon exactly as it was, I might choose one where nothing important happened and you were there for all of it.
This is the sample letter that ships with the museum. In the private studio, you can write the words that belong here, and they will replace this page for both of us.
